newsitem.title: USA: US Airways jumps as earnings top expectations.
newsitem.headline: US Airways jumps as earnings top expectations.

text.p: Shares of US Airways Group Inc gained about 14 percent after the airline's first quarter earnings topped Wall Street expectations.
US Airways, one of the most active issues on the New York Stock Exchange, was up four poinits at 32-7/8 in afternoon trading.
Investors appeared unfazed by US Airways's announcement that it may have to downsize if it does not get a competitive cost structure in place, analysts said.
"The company has been saying this forever. A lot of it is true, but a lot of it is posturing with the pilots," said one analyst, who declined to be named.

US Airways' stronger-than-expected first quarter results may hinder talks with the pilots, analysts said. The airline is seeking a 12.5 percent pay cut from its pilots at a time when pilots at rival airlines are getting big pay increases.
"Of course it's tough to get concessions when you're outpacing analysts' estimates. But think about how profitable they would be if they had a competitive cost structure in place."
Analysts estimate the company needs to get $1.0 billion to $1.5 billion in wage, salary and productivity concessions to be in competitive with its rivals.

US Airways has managed to trim some costs. During the first quarter, US Airways's costs per available seat mile declined 3.6 percent to 12.35 cents, despite a 16.1 percent rise in the cost of aviation fuel.
US Airways also benefitted from strong demand throughout the airline industry and higher fares.

"It's a combination of demand and controlling costs. Costs continue to get better," said Susan Donofrio, an airline analyst with NatWest Securities. "We expect this strength to continue through to the second quarter."

Donofrio said she raised her second quarter earnings estimate to $2.00 a share from $1.50 a share. On a consensus basis, analysts expect US Airways' second quarter results to be $1.77 a share, falling short of last year's $1.91 a share.
